proportion of type i), the replicator equation ˙xi = xi(Ax)i −xT Ax specifies the derivative of the
frequency of a type i (The Euclidean norm of the derivative is plotted as flow strength). As xT Ax
is the mean population fitness and (Ax)i is the expected payoff of type i, this equation compares
individual frequencies against the population mean. Per this model, the frequency of a given type
increases if it has higher fitness than the population mean, and decreases if it has lower fitness. The
system’s attractors, stable points where frequencies stop changing, reveal which strategy combinations
coexist in equilibrium. The dynamics of this system can reveal which strategies are evolutionarily
stable and produce approximate equilibria.
